dataset_verdict.pipeline_complete: generate -> compile -> preflight-capable synthesize -> measure -> tokenize, 264/264 rows, 0 failures
dataset_verdict.what_that_means: Every measured cell came out under 10 us, i.e. in the regime 6.6.1 showed is majority LAUNCHER: ~1.3 us of irreducible dispatch plus single-launch measurement overhead against a 2.4-6.5 us total. The measured medians therefore carry real signal about the LAUNCH PATH and very little about the kernel body. This dataset is valid and it is NOT the dataset the 9.x model wants -- the sweep's top size (2^18) is still too small to leave the launcher.
dataset_verdict.op_signal: per-op medians span 0.0030-0.0035 ms -- a 17% spread across eight arithmetic ops, which at this size is within the launch-dominated scatter rather than an op effect
dataset_verdict.size_signal: median rises 0.0030 -> 0.0038 ms from n=2^12 to 2^18, i.e. the only clean trend in the batch, and it is the trend a launcher-dominated measurement would NOT show
dataset_verdict.next_step: Extend the size sweep to 2^22-2^24 (which is where 6.6.2's anchor read 1576 GB/s) so rows land in the >=10 us regime. That is a manifest change and a re-run, not a code change, and the GPU-side cost is bounded by the same precompile-then-measure split used here.
